status: PASS all27 sealed-v3 global physical maps
findings: No mismatch, overlapping reserved waves, programmed-page escape, missing/duplicated row interval, input-dimension discrepancy, cross-layer expert-ID collision or byte-ledger error found in the27 generated maps.

The audit never imports the root compiler or backend allocator. For each layer it derives full-row job semantics from native arrays offsets/jobs/input_columns/total_rows and known model shape, then compares that derivation with both local and merged global logical records.

For each expert/projection, offsets form nonempty consecutive slices covering every job once. C equals the full input dimension; row_start is independently reconstructed by cumulative native job rows. Every matrix covers its exact full output range once, and every full-row command fits one block-index bundle.

All global physical jobs match their array-derived chip, pages and ordinary-read waves. Start plane is0; page order is wordline-major and plane=page_index%planes. Reserved half-open wordline intervals are sorted per chip/block and checked disjoint. Both all padded programmed pages and useful coefficient bytes lie within the native block boundary.

Global block IDs are contiguous on each chip. Independently count block-index bundles and compute payload/pages/reserved-wave/allocated-block bytes. These four byte ledgers exactly match both physical document and model_totals.json for all27 cases.
Expected coefficient payload equals layers*3*D*(E*I+shared_I) for every family/command. This includes the single merged shared expert per MoE layer; no extra model component is silently counted.

Training selection identities are identical across all layers of each model/command/family. The64 selection routes are checked against original already-existing route arrays using both saved subsampling index lists and real physical-layer indices. Summing saved per-layer costs gives exactly the saved global selection-cost vector, mean and P99. These are aggregate FFN service sums rather than full-model time.
limits: The unit chip_blocks counts one same-address bundle of planes native blocks, not a single native plane block. Allocated bytes use block_wordlines*planes*page_bytes per bundle.

There is no supplied physical-device budget; these are legal virtual simultaneous-resident coefficient address maps and ledgers, not verified fit on a particular device. SLC/LSB naming is a modeled accessible-capacity convention, not a new flash-mode capability.
Best-fit decreasing is one legal packing heuristic. This audit does not prove minimum block count or infeasibility for tighter capacity.

Actual coefficient byte payload/programming, activation/scale ABI and PE numerical output are not tested. Row-scale metadata stays in host DRAM under the declared contract and is excluded from coefficient-page ledgers. Attention/router/SSM, non-MoE initial dense layers, allocator/FTL overprovisioning and other model weights are also excluded.

The known imported-plan physical metadata validation bug can accept inconsistent hand-edited logical metadata in the audited old backend. The generated v3 arrays and logical records are consistent, as independently checked here; root will fix the general import guard separately.

V3 search attribution contains family aliases with separate fitting budgets. Correct address maps and service sums do not validate the claimed geometric source of a family improvement. Root is separately deduplicating complete variant-array geometries; no novel-geometry or heldout-speed claim is made here.

The initial independent audit script had a list/dict lookup mistake for selection metadata after the first map geometry checks. That own-script failure and original frozen protocol are retained under audit-attempt-v1; the corrected source received a fresh protocol before the full successful run.
